subject: biology

items.q: Which variable do you change in an experiment?
items.why: You change the independent variable and measure its effect on the dependent variable.

items.q: How do you make results more reliable?
items.correct: Repeat readings and calculate a mean.
items.misconception: Do the experiment only once, quickly.
items.why: Repeats and a mean reduce the effect of random error and reveal anomalies.

items.correct: Only the independent variable changes; other variables are controlled.
items.misconception: You change as many variables as possible.
items.why: Controlling other variables ensures any change in the result is due to the independent variable.

items.q: What should you do with a clear anomalous result?
items.correct: Identify it and usually exclude it from the mean.
items.misconception: Always include it in the mean.
items.random_wrong: Repeat the whole experiment from scratch.
items.why: Anomalies that don't fit the pattern are normally left out of the mean (and ideally investigated).
